approaches.name: Integrated digital financial, M&E and GIS data platforms for local councils
approaches.description: The project builds web-based financial, M&E and GIS platforms so councils and ministries share real-time budget, project and service-delivery data. Practices: web-based PETRA/PFM Smart financial management system for LCs; automated project database for council public investment programme; Audit Management Information System for local government audits; NaMEMIS integrated M&E data platform linking MDAs, LCs, NGOs; GIS-enabled web portal for LC data posting and central feedback; Automated data platforms for education and health supply inputs; Digitized SOPs and M&E data-flow systems across national, district, community levels; Online/offline data platforms for last-mile commodity distribution tracking; Real-time GIS-tagged service delivery dashboards with citizen input; GEMS field-appropriate digital data collection for M&E; NaMED data platform for monthly local council reporting of textbook, TLM and drug distribution; NaMED/NaMEMIS data platform with web/phone feedback portal for registered users; NaMED platform for monthly textbook and drug distribution reporting; NaMED web/phone portal for user feedback on service data; Live web-based LC financial system for real-time expenditure tracking; Geo-enabled Monitoring and Supervision (GEMS) for beneficiary surveys.

extra_evidence.text: This sub‐component will focus on strengthening key PFM functions to support basic service delivery , including through improved tools, procedures, and skills building for central- and local-level staff.

Project would finance the development of guidelines, templates and related guidance for the preparation of the PIP, the implementation of an automated project database for Councils, and initiatives to promote and facilitate the participation of private sector in public investment and capital projects across all councils.

Strengthening ASSL's capacity to undertake timely audits of all local government financial statements through the implementation of an Audit Management Information System (AMIS) and enhance capacity of the IT unit within ASSL to support a more efficient audit process.

NaMED aims towards a National Monitoring and Evaluation Management Information System (NaMEMIS) that can link the monitoring units of MDAs, LCs, contractors, non-governmental organizations (NGOs), and donor-funded projects.

The project will support the Government’s proposed reforms to improve data management and reporting at the local level through targeted support to LCs, as well as data on critical service-delivery inputs in the priority sectors of education and health.

Through the Directorate of Science, Technology and Innovation (DSTI), the government has already invested in several innovative digital platforms (e.g., Education Data Hub) to support service delivery.

This system is proposed to be a Geographic Information System (GIS)-enabled, web-based internet portal onto which LCs are expected to post their data and reports, but also from which they may access information on actions taken at the central level regarding their local area.

(ii) support to data management platforms covering the distribution of key sectoral critical inputs in education (text books, TLM) and health (drugs, medical supplies and equipment); and (iii) technical and operational support to the NaMED in its collaboration with DSTI and other key sector MDAs (Health, Education, and Local Government) to provide technical leadership for simplified, streamlined and automated data platforms for monitoring and accountability (NaMESIS) and support wider public awareness and citizen engagement on use of such monitoring data.
The component will address three different levels of support : (i) Support to LCs as conveners of data on service delivery investments and performance at the local level;

Project activities include: • Supporting the role District Councils play in reporting on district-level investment and service performance in education (engaging District Education Offices (DEOs)), and health (engaging District Health Management Teams (DHMTs); while also supporting community-level structures as conveners of community participation on issues development results and of budget transparency alongside participatory/third-party monitoring and reporting). • Supporting improved monitoring of development interventions through digitized standard operating procedures/tools, M&E systems and operational plans that focus on standardizing the management of data flows between the national (NaMEMIS), district councils and community structures. • Supporting communications and outreach interventions (TV, radio, SMS, targeted messaging) to promote community engagement in basic services delivery and inform local decision making.

(ii) TLM, (iii) drugs; and (iv) medical supplies and equipment. • Supporting the design and roll-out of innovative digital and offline/online data platforms that work with, and improve, existing data management information system with NMSA, MoHS and Ministry of Basic and Senior Secondary Education (MBSSE).

It will aim to strengthen data availability for LCs in their role in overseeing and protecting the distribution of key critical inputs in the ‘last mile’ of the supply chain by: • Strengthening. the collaboration between the NaMED, DSTI, and the health and education ministries to improve the data collection, recording, control, and reporting of distribution on: (i) textbooks;
Data platforms will cover collection of real-time data for effective monitoring, including GIS-tagging, to facilitate a more robust supply chain.

Data platforms, including service deliver y dashboards, will be designed to allow input from citizens, District and Ward M&E Committees, and community- based organizations (CBOs). • Supporting the design and roll-out of innovative digital and offline/online data platforms that work with, and improve, existing data management information system with NMSA and MBSSE.
Data platforms including service delivery dashboard, will be designed to allow input from citizens, District and Ward M&E Committees, and CBOs.
A key activity under this component is the implementation and operation of a robust M&E system supported by using a field-appropriate technology GEMS for digital data collection and analysis.

approaches.name: e-Procurement, GEMS monitoring and linked data platforms for accountability
approaches.description: The project rolls out e-GP, open contracting and GEMS feedback tools and links council and ministry platforms to NaMEMIS for two-way data flows. Practices: e-Government Procurement rollout in health and education; e-Procurement and open contracting with supplier database; Linking local and MDA data platforms to umbrella NaMEMIS; e-Procurement system roll-out for health and education; GEMS system for subproject monitoring and citizen feedback; GEMS platform collecting citizen feedback on local investments; e-GP procurement transactions tracked in health and education; E-procurement and framework contracts for council procurement.
approaches.why_innovative: New process: e-procurement transactions in priority sectors - cue: 'implementation of e-Procurement' | category Operational; adoption apply; judged in 1 round(s); final check: digital core, in_use before 2019

evidence.text: 12 The overall sub- component objective is to increase the transparency and accountability in government procurement system through the implementation of e-Procurement (e-GP), with the focus of the project delivering results in the key priority sectors of education (textbooks, teaching and learning material - TLM) and health (drugs, medical supplies and equipment).

extra_evidence.text: The project-supported activities will be part of the wider e-GP roll out strategy of the NPPA for the strengthening of procurement systems reforms in all ministries, departments, and agencies (MDAs).

The sub-component activities will be aimed towards mainstreaming of e-Procurement and open contracting and its operationalization in the education and health sectors through an increased number of procurement transactions using the e-GP system.

Key activities would include: • The preparation and implementation of an action plan, including change management, roll-out, and adoption of e-Procurement in the health and education sectors. • E-GP tender process completed and operationalization of the e-Procurement system. • Transitioning existing manual procurement processes (e.g., increased training of procurement practitioners – controllers and suppliers) – developing the supplier database. • E-Procurement training and capacity building of relevant stakeholders in the education and health sectors. • Implementation of e-Procurement awareness and sensitization. • Change management support, including staffing of the e-Procurement Directorate in the NPPA.

Page 25 of 104 The World Bank Accountable Governance for Basic Service Delivery (P172492) Sub-component 3.3: Supporting the demonstration effect of using data platforms for results reporting and decision- making at local level to support development and operationalization of NaMEMIS (IDA: US$0.70 million) • Strengthening NaMED and DSTI through its collaborations with key sector MDAs (Education and Health) to deliver simplified, streamlined and automated data platforms that support monitoring and accountability. • Supporting the use of data platforms by LCs and central MDAs overseeing management of basic services in education and health as a demonstration effect for an umbrella NaMEMIS. • Link data platforms used by LCs and MDAs to NaMEMIS to ensure data flows from the national to the subnational and vice-versa, so that development decisions at the local level are linked to the national development plan. • Strengthening service delivery transparency through publication of regular, easy-to-use, monitoring reports (e.g., summary on use of funds against results achieved and record of implementation progress on investment projects at the local level) • Supporting NaMED’s engagement

For instance: Sub-component 1.2 will support roll-out of an e-Procurement system for health and education, while concurrent TA support through Sub-component 3.2 will support the local level by building better systems to oversee and monitor the distribution of procured goods (the 'last mile' of local service delivery).
The project M&E plan for implementation of Development Grants would be enhanced by the design and implementation of a GEMS system.

The project M&E team would collect data at subproject level through quarterly Page 34 of 104 The World Bank Accountable Governance for Basic Service Delivery (P172492) physical and financial progress submitted by LCs, complemented with the use of field-appropriate technology for digital data collection and analysis.
The use of GEMS would not only support the monitoring of physical progress, but it would also allow to collect citizens ’ feedback on local investments financed under the project.
The project will finance the costs of implementing GEMS that include consultancies, logistics and other equipment.
